core_obligations: Separate the cases: if some quasi-compact open neighbourhood of one point is disjoint from some quasi-compact open neighbourhood of the other, the second alternative holds (proof lines 4721-4728)
Otherwise intersect: the pairwise intersections of the two neighbourhood families are nonempty, and they are closed in the constructible topology (proof lines 4729-4732)

Conclude: compactness of the constructible topology and the finite intersection criterion give a point in the total intersection, which specializes to both points because the families are fundamental systems of neighbourhoods and the space is sober (proof lines 4733-4738)
proof_roadmap: 取 {U_i} 为 x 的准紧开邻域族（有限交仍是其中一员），{V_j} 同理。
若某个 U_i ∩ V_j = ∅ ⇒ 得不相交开邻域。
否则所有 U_i ∩ V_j 非空，且在可构造拓扑中闭；由可构造拓扑紧 + 有限交判据，∩(U_i ∩ V_j) 非空；由 sober 与「{U_i} 是 x 的基本邻域系」，∩U_i 恰是 x 的一般化集合，故该点同时特殊化到 x 与 y。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that for two points of a spectral space either there is a third point specializing to both or the two points have disjoint open neighbourhoods (author lemma at source lines 4714-4719, label lemma-two-points). The proof (source lines 4721-4739) takes the families of quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of the two points, separates off the disjoint case and otherwise uses compactness of the constructible topology to produce a point in the total intersection, which specializes to both (proof lines 4721-4738). The compactness argument on the constructible topology is the substance. H3.
